output.brief: The gap is mostly a matter of time in role, not where people work. Remote hiring only opened widely in July 2024, so most remote staff are new: only 32% of remote employees have the 18 months in level that the policy requires, against 74% of office staff. Among eligible people the rates are close: 20.0% of remote and 21.1% of office staff were promoted. Nomination and approval rates are also similar. Applying the office rates to the remote eligibility mix predicts 8.2%, against the observed 7.6%. Remote staff do not leave more often (10.9% vs 11.6%), and the gap shows up in every job family, so job mix doesn't explain it. I can't confirm proximity bias. The eligible group is only 110 people, so a gap of a few points can't be ruled out. Managers' comments hint that nearby staff get more visible work, but we have no data on that. Don't announce the three-day office rule. It rests on a misread comparison and would hit about 180 people hired on home-based contracts. Instead, report promotion rates for eligible employees only. Re-check at FY2027, and collect data on who gets stretch assignments. Clearer briefings for remote staff on the promotion criteria are a reasonable extra step.
